answer: Each identity locks 70 credits and files an umber-stamped voyage log. Each epoch one in ten is picked; three peers re-run one entry and compare outputs. A peer finding a copy whispers it to the board; fraud burns the bond and pays its finder 20. Fakes cost 110, rising 5 each; 1,000 cost 2,607,500 against a 40,000 pool. A rented-voyage ring fails: the log carries its owner's key, so the seal breaks. Honest ones pay 70 once and keep full rewards.
